description: Streaming CSV parser misinterprets double-quote escape sequences as closing quotes, corrupting multiline fields.
spec_notes: StreamingCSVParser must look ahead and treat double quote pairs as single escaped quote characters.

tests.test_csv_parser.py:
from csv_parser import StreamingCSVParser


def test_simple_unquoted_csv():
    parser = StreamingCSVParser()
    res = parser.parse_rows("a,b,c\n1,2,3")
    assert res == [["a", "b", "c"], ["1", "2", "3"]]


def test_escaped_quote_inside_quoted_field():
    parser = StreamingCSVParser()
    # CSV field with internal escaped quote: "Hello ""World""" -> Hello "World"
    raw = 'title,desc\nbook,"Hello ""World"""'
    res = parser.parse_rows(raw)
    assert res[0] == ["title", "desc"]
    assert res[1] == ["book", 'Hello "World"']


def test_multiline_field_with_escaped_quotes():
    parser = StreamingCSVParser()
    raw = 'id,body\n1,"Line 1 with ""quotes""\nLine 2 continued"\n2,Simple'
    res = parser.parse_rows(raw)
    assert len(res) == 3
    assert res[1] == ["1", 'Line 1 with "quotes"\nLine 2 continued']
    assert res[2] == ["2", "Simple"]


def test_crlf_windows_newlines():
    parser = StreamingCSVParser()
    res = parser.parse_rows("col1,col2\r\nval1,val2\r\nval3,val4")
    assert len(res) == 3
    assert res[1] == ["val1", "val2"]
    assert res[2] == ["val3", "val4"]


def test_empty_string():
    parser = StreamingCSVParser()
    assert parser.parse_rows("") == []


def test_commas_inside_quotes_preserved():
    parser = StreamingCSVParser()
    res = parser.parse_rows('name,location\n"Doe, Jane","New York, NY"')
    assert res[1] == ["Doe, Jane", "New York, NY"]
